title: Phase-stable voltage bias for Josephson photonics devices
authors: Amir Hosein Esmaeili, Naveen Nehra, Alexandre Paquette, Mona Arabmohammadi, Baptiste Monge, Alexandre Rogalle, Francois Cyrenne-Bergeron, Yannick Lapointe, Nicolas Lavoie, Nicolas Bourlet, Max Hofheinz
abstract: Parametric interactions are foundational to superconducting quantum technologies, yet conventional microwave-driven pumping introduces parasitic Kerr nonlinearities and higher-order harmonics that limit device performance. Josephson Photonics (JP) avoids these parasitics by utilizing dc-biased junctions but has remained constrained by high phase noise and the absence of a stable phase reference. Here, we overcome this limitation by integrating a Josephson voltage standard (JVS) to establish a noise-tolerant phase reference, and demonstrate that this reference is coherently transferred to an inelastic Cooper-pair tunneling amplifier (ICTA) via the superconducting order parameter.The resulting low-phase-noise architecture yields a 14-dB enhancement in averaged gain and better quantum-limited noise performance. Critically, the phase reference enables the first observation of phase-sensitive gain and sqeezing in a dc-biased amplifier. By reconciling clean, Kerr-free nonlinearities with phase-coherent drive, our architecture establishes a robust platform for high-purity parametric processes in superconducting circuits.
summary: The researchers developed a novel architecture by coupling a Josephson Voltage Standard (JVS) to a Josephson Photonics amplifier (ICTA) to solve the problem of phase noise. This integration successfully establishes a stable phase reference, leading to a significant gain enhancement and enabling the first demonstration of phase-sensitive quantum effects like squeezing in a dc-biased superconducting amplifier.
main_problem: Conventional parametric pumping methods suffer from parasitic nonlinearities, and existing Josephson Photonics (JP) devices lack a stable phase reference necessary for phase-coherent operation.
main_result: By integrating a Josephson Voltage Standard (JVS) to provide a noise-tolerant phase reference, the authors achieved a 14-dB gain enhancement and enabled the first observation of phase-sensitive gain and squeezing in a dc-biased amplifier.
method: The study involves characterizing the Interacting Cavity Transmission Amplifier (ICTA) using gain maps and phase-space analysis, comparing performance with and without the active JVS reference.
model_or_system: The system utilizes Josephson Junctions forming an ICTA, which is coupled to a JVS. The physics is described by Josephson junction potentials and analyzed using quantum Langevin equations and phase-space diagnostics.
key_observables: Averaged gain (up to 27 dB), quantum-limited noise performance, phase-sensitive gain, and squeezing characteristics.
important_parameters: DC bias voltage, RF tone power ($P_{JVS}$), signal frequency ($f_S$), and the phase difference ($\Delta$) between the signal and the phase reference.
main_assumptions: The phase reference from the JVS is assumed to be coherently transferred to the ICTA via the superconducting order parameter, and phase noise averaging is assumed when the JVS is off.
figures_summary: Figures compare ICTA gain and noise with and without JVS stabilization, showing phase-space distributions that transition from phase-preserving (JVS off) to phase-sensitive (JVS on).
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitations of JP devices, then introduces the JVS-ICTA architecture. It proceeds to characterize the gain and noise in different regimes (degenerate vs. non-degenerate), demonstrating the critical role of the JVS in stabilizing the phase reference and enabling phase-sensitive quantum effects.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the challenge of phase coherence in superconducting quantum circuits, which is crucial for realizing high-fidelity quantum light sources and parametric processes.
